title: 0046-analysis-of-points-outcome-in-atp
universal_lens: Bayesian optimal prediction of tennis point outcomes reduces to server win probability, with no added value from accumulated match statistics or serve placement features due to conditional independence and high noise.
gsi_mapping: GSI receives noisy binary observations of tennis points; the optimal Bayesian predictive distribution collapses to a degenerate point-mass at the server's empirical win rate, rendering all covariates useless for improving probabilistic forecasts.
gse_mapping: GSE models tennis points as a memoryless state-transition process where the server's baseline win probability is the only invariant feature; any additional state variables (e.g., accumulated games) do not alter the transition kernel and thus offer no tactical advantage.

primitives.verbatim_quote: # [0046] Analysis of points outcome in ATP Grand Slam Tennis using big data and machine learning (arXiv:2506.05866v1) **Citation:** Martin Illum, Hans Christian Bechsøfft Mikkelsen, Emil Hovad (2025).
primitives.assumptions: Point outcomes are conditionally independent given the serve type and the server's inherent skill; accumulated match statistics provide no additional predictive power beyond the raw server win rate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High noise regime where the signal-to-noise ratio of covariates is negligible compared to the natural variance in tennis scoring.

layer2.mapping: The optimal conformal predictor for tennis point outcomes is identical to the historical server win frequency, establishing a duality between GSI's market equilibrium and this baseline.
layer2.telemetry: Observed server win rates (73.2% first serve, 57.2% second serve) as the empirical Bayes estimate under squared loss.

primitives.name: No Additive Value of Covariates
primitives.verbatim_quote: # [0046] Analysis of points outcome in ATP Grand Slam Tennis using big data and machine learning (arXiv:2506.05866v1) **Citation:** Martin Illum, Hans Christian Bechsøfft Mikkelsen, Emil Hovad (2025).
primitives.assumptions: The dataset contains only pre-point features; post-point outcomes are shifted to avoid lookahead bias; the true data-generating process already incorporates all available information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As the sample size grows, the out-of-sample performance of any model converges to the baseline, indicating that the observed data provides no incremental information structure.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, this primitive maps to the principle that static match statistics cannot improve dynamic trajectory predictions because the game dynamics are memoryless relative to the server's skill.
layer2.telemetry: Model accuracy metrics (e.g., AUC) are near 0.5, equivalent to random guessing, confirming the absence of exploitable patterns in the covariates.

layer2.telemetry: The best F1-score is achieved by predicting the majority class (server wins) with minimal recall, demonstrating the degeneracy of the learning problem.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core failure mode is that tennis point outcomes are governed by a latent skill variable (server quality) that subsumes all observable covariates. Pre-point accumulators like aces or double faults are merely proxies for this underlying ability, leading to perfect collinearity. Consequently, any machine learning model regressing these proxies will simply re-estimate the marginal server win rate, yielding no new information. This is a classic case of over-parameterization without identifiability, resulting in a flat likelihood surface where the baseline model maximizes both training and test performance.
